entity.summary: Crypto-asset wallet and trading service combining lending, custodial account and wallet functions, crypto-to-crypto swapping, card purchase access, and a project model that describes smart-contract-based permissionless finance. After account-level transfer and withdrawal restrictions began in August 2026, Japan's Financial Services Agency published a warning concerning Izakaya Limited on 2026-09-01. On 2026-09-17 IZAKA-YA announced that service for all Japan residents and Japanese nationals living abroad would end, with new registrations and new lending stopped for affected users and a withdrawal-only process remaining available. HEI therefore classifies the exchange service as limited rather than globally dead.
entity.notes: The current first-party service exposes account-based wallet, lending, swap and crypto-purchase functions. First-party project documentation describes permissionless smart-contract-based lending, swap and token-management architecture, while the live support surface documents email/password accounts, managed balances, internal transfers and service-side transaction history. HEI therefore uses hybrid rather than classifying the service as purely centralized or purely decentralized. The first-party company page identifies Izakaya Limited and a Hong Kong operating address, supporting Hong Kong as country_or_origin. It states a service start month of December 2023, but because no exact day is established HEI leaves launch_date null. On 2026-08-24 the operator announced mandatory KYC and temporary transfer/withdrawal restrictions for some investigated accounts; on 2026-08-27 and 2026-09-07 it continued to state that restrictions were not universal and that reviewed transactions were being processed individually. Japan's Financial Services Agency published on 2026-09-01 that it had issued a warning concerning Izakaya Limited for unregistered crypto-asset exchange business. On 2026-09-17 IZAKA-YA announced that it would end service for all Japan residents and Japanese nationals abroad, stop new registration and new lending for the affected population, close the Japanese-language site at the end of September, and keep the withdrawal procedure available until asset-return handling is completed. HEI records these developments as a regional/regulatory service restriction. It does not infer a global shutdown, insolvency, universal withdrawal failure, criminal conduct, or completed customer repayment beyond what the cited sources establish.

events.title: IZAKA-YA and CryptoPanda ran linked-service collaboration campaign
events.description: IZAKA-YA published a collaboration campaign requiring users to register with both services, link IZAKA-YA with CryptoPanda, and complete a CryptoPanda transaction connected to an IZAKA-YA wallet.
events.notes: The event establishes a documented service integration/collaboration. HEI uses the existing `other` event type because the projected event enum does not define a dedicated partnership value. It does not imply common ownership, merger, acquisition, predecessor/successor status, or that the two services are the same entity.

events.title: IZAKA-YA documented its KYC boundary for lending and swaps
events.description: IZAKA-YA stated that ordinary lending and in-platform swap services remain usable without identity verification while KYC is required for campaign participation.
events.notes: Recorded as a material operating-policy event. HEI does not infer regulatory compliance, non-compliance, licence status, or safety from the operator's KYC statement alone.

events.title: IZAKA-YA disclosed temporary transfer and withdrawal restrictions for some accounts
events.description: IZAKA-YA stated that suspected illicit-fund inflows or money-laundering signals had been identified in some transactions and that affected accounts were temporarily restricted from transfers and withdrawals while being investigated. The operator stated that this was not a uniform platform-wide halt and that ordinary transfers and withdrawals could also take longer during enhanced monitoring.
events.notes: Records the operator's first-party notice and its stated scope. HEI does not infer insolvency, a universal withdrawal freeze, customer loss, or criminal conduct by any specific user from this notice alone. The same notice also changed the previously stated KYC boundary by announcing mandatory KYC for all IZAKA-YA users.

events.title: CryptoPanda terminated its IZAKA-YA partnership and wallet integration
events.description: CryptoPanda announced that it had ended its partnership with IZAKA-YA and that transactions through IZAKA-YA wallet connections would no longer be available, removing a previously documented linked-service transaction route.
events.notes: This records a counterparty's first-party announcement and the loss of a documented integration route. CryptoPanda cited information raising AML-related concerns about IZAKA-YA; HEI does not convert that stated rationale into an independently established AML finding or infer a platform-wide IZAKA-YA withdrawal failure from it.

events.title: IZAKA-YA reported sequential withdrawal and transfer processing after individual checks
events.description: IZAKA-YA stated that no platform-wide transfer or withdrawal halt was in place, that transfers had been made to some customers whose reviews were completed on 2026-08-25, and that additional cases continued to be processed after individual checks.
events.notes: The event records the operator's current status statement. It does not independently verify completion times for all customers, establish that every restricted account has been restored, or resolve third-party reports of withdrawal problems.

events.title: Japan FSA published warning concerning Izakaya Limited
events.description: Japan's Financial Services Agency published that it had issued a warning to Izakaya Limited concerning unregistered crypto-asset exchange business in Japan.
events.notes: This records the regulator's published warning. HEI does not treat the warning alone as proof of insolvency, fraud, or a global service shutdown.

events.title: IZAKA-YA said some withdrawals remained under enhanced review
events.description: IZAKA-YA stated that some customer withdrawals and transfers remained subject to additional KYC, transaction-history, destination-address, source-of-funds and related compliance checks, while again saying that withdrawals were not uniformly stopped for all customers.
events.notes: First-party status update only. It does not independently verify completion times for affected customers or establish that every reported withdrawal problem was resolved.

events.title: IZAKA-YA announced service termination for Japan-targeted customers
events.description: IZAKA-YA announced that service would end for all customers residing in Japan regardless of nationality and for Japanese nationals living abroad. It said new registration and new lending would stop for the affected population, the Japanese-language site would close at the end of September, and the withdrawal procedure would remain available until asset-return handling was completed.
events.notes: This is a regional and nationality-scoped shutdown announcement, not evidence that IZAKA-YA has ended service globally. HEI keeps the entity limited and leaves death_reason and death_date unset pending evidence of a terminal global shutdown.

evidence.title: IZAKA-YA public service site
evidence.notes: Current first-party site presents active lending, crypto-to-crypto swap, wallet and crypto-purchase functions. Promotional yield, security and compliance claims are not independently adopted by HEI.

evidence.title: IZAKA-YA company profile
evidence.notes: First-party company page identifies Izakaya Limited, a Hong Kong operating address and a December 2023 service start month. HEI uses the operator/location evidence for country_or_origin but does not invent an exact launch day.

evidence.title: IZAKA-YA project purpose
evidence.notes: First-party project documentation describes permissionless smart-contract-based lending, swapping and token management. Used to support the hybrid service classification; forward-looking ecosystem claims are not treated as completed features unless corroborated by the live service.

evidence.title: How to use the IZAKA-YA wallet
evidence.notes: Official support documentation states that users can manage cryptocurrencies, lend, swap, deposit, send and review balances/transaction history through the service.

evidence.title: IZAKAYA x CryptoPanda IZKY token campaign
evidence.notes: First-party campaign page documents linked registration and a CryptoPanda transaction connected to an IZAKA-YA wallet. Used to establish the collaboration/integration event only.

evidence.title: 〖重要〗IZAKA-YAのKYC（本人確認）について〖結論：キャンペーン時のみ必須〗
evidence.notes: First-party statement that standard lending and swap use does not require KYC and that campaign participation does. HEI records the policy statement without converting it into a legal conclusion.

evidence.title: 送金・出金およびKYC認証に関するお知らせ
evidence.notes: First-party notice states that some accounts were temporarily restricted from transfers and withdrawals during investigation of transactions suspected of illicit-fund or money-laundering involvement, while explicitly stating that the measure was not a uniform platform-wide halt. It also announces mandatory KYC for all users and warns that ordinary transfer/withdrawal processing may take longer.

evidence.title: レンディングの利回りはどこから捻出されているのでしょうか？
evidence.notes: First-party support says customer assets are operated through OTC and DEX activity and that part of resulting operating profit is returned as lending yield. HEI preserves this as an operator explanation only; the public article does not provide independently verifiable trading volume, realized profit, counterparties, deployment balances, or a reconciliation demonstrating the source or sustainability of ordinary or promotional yields.

evidence.title: 提携解消のお知らせ
evidence.notes: Counterparty first-party notice ending the IZAKA-YA partnership and disabling IZAKA-YA wallet-connected transactions. The notice's AML-related rationale is treated as CryptoPanda's stated reason, not an independently established finding.

evidence.title: 出金・送金に関する現在の対応状況およびSNS上の情報について
evidence.notes: First-party follow-up states that there is no universal withdrawal/transfer halt, that some reviewed transfers were completed on 2026-08-25, and that remaining cases are being processed after individual checks. HEI preserves this as the operator's current-status statement rather than treating it as independent proof that all withdrawal issues are resolved.

evidence.title: Izakaya Limitedに対する警告書の発出について
evidence.notes: Official FSA publication index records the 2026-09-01 publication of a warning concerning Izakaya Limited for unregistered crypto-asset exchange business.

evidence.title: 出金・送金に関する確認状況およびコンプライアンス対応について
evidence.notes: First-party update states that some withdrawals/transfers remained under enhanced individual review and that withdrawals were not uniformly stopped for all users.

evidence.title: 〖重要〗日本居住者の皆様へのサービス提供終了および預かり資産の出金手続きについて
evidence.notes: First-party notice establishes the Japan-resident/Japanese-national service termination scope, stop on new registration and lending for affected users, planned Japanese-site closure, and continued withdrawal procedure. It does not establish a global IZAKA-YA shutdown.
